colors-1-usage-scene-1.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares red, blue, and yellow colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a colour like a clear daytime sky.
colors-1-usage-scene-1.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: the color of a ripe tomato; the color of a clear daytime sky; the color of a ripe lemon. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-1-usage-scene-2.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares green, orange, and purple colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a bright colour often used on high-visibility clothing.
colors-1-usage-scene-2.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: the color of fresh grass; the color of ripe citrus peel; the color of many violet petals. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-1-usage-scene-3.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares pink, brown, and black colour samples. The final choice must match this description: the darkest common colour, often used for strong text.
colors-1-usage-scene-3.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a light rosy flower color; the color of natural wood bark; the appearance of near-total darkness. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-1-usage-scene-4.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares white, cyan, and magenta colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a bright blue-green colour used in printing and screens.
colors-1-usage-scene-4.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: the color of fresh snow; a bright blue-green sample; a vivid reddish-purple sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-1-usage-scene-5.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares lime, teal, and indigo colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a deep blue-violet colour.
colors-1-usage-scene-5.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a bright yellow-green sample; a dark blue-green sample; a deep blue-violet sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-2-usage-scene-1.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares violet, coral, and salmon colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a blue-purple colour near the end of the visible spectrum.
colors-2-usage-scene-1.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a blue-purple sample; a warm red-orange sample; a pale reddish-orange sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-2-usage-scene-2.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares turquoise, lavender, and light colour samples. The final choice must match this description: a pale purple colour.
colors-2-usage-scene-2.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a bright greenish-blue sample; a pale purple sample; a high-lightness gray-blue sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-2-usage-scene-3.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares dark, bright, and dull colour samples. The final choice must match this description: not bright or vivid.
colors-2-usage-scene-3.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a very low-lightness blue sample; a high-intensity rosy sample; a low-intensity gray-rose sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-2-usage-scene-4.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares vivid, pale, and deep colour samples. The final choice must match this description: light and not strongly coloured.
colors-2-usage-scene-4.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a strongly saturated rosy sample; a low-color-intensity light rose sample; a dark rich rosy sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-2-usage-scene-5.reviewedScenario: At a design review, an adult client compares warm, cool, and neutral colour samples. The final choice must match this description: visually associated with blues or greens.
colors-2-usage-scene-5.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a reddish-yellow sample; a blue-toned sample; a gray-beige sample. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-3-usage-scene-1.reviewedScenario: At a print and design studio, an adult designer needs to mix two colours, blend neighbouring colours, and choose a darker shade. For the next step, the brief gives this description: combine colours smoothly so the transition is less visible.
colors-3-usage-scene-1.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: two differently colored paint circles overlapping to produce a third color; a smooth transition between neighboring colors; versions of one color progressing from lighter to darker. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-3-usage-scene-2.reviewedScenario: At a print and design studio, an adult designer needs to add a light tint, compare the hue, and adjust the saturation. For the next step, the brief gives this description: a lighter version or touch of a colour.
colors-3-usage-scene-2.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: versions of one color progressing toward white; three equally strong different colors; versions of blue progressing from muted gray-blue to vivid blue. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-3-usage-scene-3.reviewedScenario: At a print and design studio, an adult designer needs to apply a smooth gradient and use a rainbow reference. For the next step, the brief gives this description: a natural arc showing several colours after light is split by water droplets.
colors-3-usage-scene-3.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: a continuous transition across several colors; seven nested colored arcs in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and purple order. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.

colors-3-usage-scene-4.reviewedScenario: At a print and design studio, an adult designer needs to check a colour spectrum and test a paint pigment. For the next step, the brief gives this description: a coloured substance used in paint, ink, or material.
colors-3-usage-scene-4.imageAlt: Design samples, left to right: adjacent color bands spanning red to purple; colored grains heaped in a shallow dish. Each sample has equal visual emphasis.
